title: journald-growth-kubelet-eviction-oncall-log
content:
Summary:

This doc captures the on-call notes and initial post-incident thinking for the 2024-11-11 morning incident where several worker nodes entered disk-pressure eviction cycles and a subset of control-plane controllers lagged, causing scheduling backlogs. Symptoms looked like a cascade: rapid growth of /var/lib/journald and /var/lib/kubelet, kubelet started evicting pods, containerd started failing container GC, and kube-controller-manager observed etcd write latency spikes. Some pods repeatedly rescheduled and created orphaned ephemeral volumes.

Impact:
- ~12 worker nodes across two AZs reported NodeCondition=DiskPressure and triggered soft evictions.
- ~180 pods were evicted over a 40-minute window; ~30 pods failed to come back cleanly (CrashLoopBackOff / CrashLoop due to missing PV mounts).
- Short-term increase in 5xx application errors for two user-facing services (approx +3% error rate for 25 minutes).
- No data loss in persistent volumes, but delayed rollouts and transient degraded latency for background jobs.

Detection and Timeline (rough):
- 06:12 UTC: Pager alert (node-disk-pressure) fired from metric rule: node_filesystem_available_bytes < threshold on several nodes.
- 06:13 UTC: First oncall message in #sre-alerts. I (Aisha) paged Miguel.
- 06:15 UTC: NodeReady flapping observed; kubelet eviction logs show pressure: "eviction manager: attempting to reclaim nodefs".
- 06:18 UTC: kubectl top nodes showed normal CPU/RAM but very low available disk on /var/lib/kubelet.
- 06:21 UTC: containerd errors in journal: "failed to update container status: no such file or directory" and later "gc: failed to remove layer: device or resource busy".
- 06:25 UTC: We discovered journald growth on nodes: /var/log/journal had a sudden multi-GB increase driven by a pattern of repeated stack traces from a log-rotate sidecar process (third-party log-collector v2.3.7) that had started spamming logs during a config reload.
- 06:30 UTC: We applied emergency remediation: rotated journal files, cleared old logs, and temporarily increased available node disk via cordon + migration to other less-used nodes.
- 06:45 UTC: Evictions slowed; kubelet GC resumed, but a subset of pods kept failing due to missing mount propagation state.

Root cause hypothesis (initial):
- Primary: A log-collector sidecar (deployed as a DaemonSet) had a regression in its config reload path that produced continuous high-volume stderr stdout logs. Those logs were sequestered by systemd-journald into /var/log/journal and journalctl's retention/size policy did not rotate aggressively enough because /etc/systemd/journald.conf had the default values (SystemMaxUse not tuned for k8s nodes). Over a few minutes this filled the ephemeral partition that backs /var/lib/kubelet (same root FS), triggering kubelet eviction manager.
- Secondary contributing factors:
  - Kubelet's eviction thresholds were conservative for our workload mix; by default the soft eviction grace periods allowed churn.
  - Containerd GC paths encountered file descriptor locks due to heavy I/O on the node, delaying image cleanup and prolonging low-free-disk state.
  - Controller-manager saw brief etcd latency spikes as it retried writes for pod status updates, which magnified scheduling delays.

Immediate mitigation steps taken (ordered):
1) Identified problematic DaemonSet (log-collector-v2) and rolled back to previous image tag on the DaemonSet (kubectl -n kube-logging set image daemonset/log-collector log-collector=log-collector:v2.3.6).
2) SSH to affected nodes and rotated journal files:
   - sudo journalctl --rotate
   - sudo journalctl --vacuum-size=500M
   - rm -f /var/log/journal/*-corrupt-*.journal (only after ensuring not in use)
3) Cordoned highest-pressure nodes and triggered pod migrations (kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force) to reduce pressure stepwise.
4) Bumped kubelet eviction thresholds temporarily (via node.kubernetes.io/eviction?): we updated the kubelet config on impacted autoscaling node pool via the node config DaemonSet to set evictionHard: {"nodefs.available":"2%"} -> 1.5% (temporary) — NOTE: this is a risky change and we reverted after stabilization.
5) Restarted containerd on two nodes where GC was stuck (sudo systemctl restart containerd) after confirming no active critical pods were on those nodes.
6) Monitored cluster health and confirmed evictions slowed and pods rejoined.

What went well:
- Fast owner detection: logs and metrics linked clearly to nodes, allowed quick pivot to journald size.
- DaemonSet rollback reduced log volume within ~4 minutes of action.
- Eviction and drain sequence prevented more critical control-plane instability; cordoning minimized scheduling thrash.

What we learned / open questions:
- Why did journald growth map onto /var/lib/kubelet quickly? Our partition layout collocates /var/log and /var/lib/kubelet on the same root partition for some older node images. We need to audit image families and ensure journal retention is tuned for node class.
- Why didn't containerd GC free space earlier? Did heavy IO lock in overlayfs prevent safe deletion? Need deeper investigation with strace on a reproduced node.
- Why did the DaemonSet emit such verbose logs on reload? Check upstream changelog for v2.3.7; there may be a known bug.

Short-term action items (owners & ETA):
- (Miguel) revert DaemonSet and create hotfix release that disables the noisy reload path; open GH PR and publish v2.3.8 hotfix. ETA 2024-11-13. (JIRA-4521)
- (Lina) Audit node image families (ami-ids) in the two affected ASGs to confirm partition layout and list nodes with /var/log collocated with kubelet. ETA 2024-11-20.
- (Oliver) Add an alert for rapid journald growth: rate_of(bytes_logged) > X over 1m for node -> alertSLO. ETA 2024-11-15.
- (Aisha) Draft node tuning change: set SystemMaxUse=1G in systemd-journald.conf for worker AMI bake; propose for review. ETA 2024-11-21.
- (Team) Add containerd GC visibility: export containerd_gc_duration_seconds and expose metrics around last_successful_gc_timestamp. ETA 2024-11-28.

Longer-term remediation ideas:
- Separate /var/log/journal onto a dedicated partition for node images (long-lead, AMI bake).
- Harden kubelet eviction configs by workload class: edge nodes vs compute nodes should have different eviction thresholds.
- Introduce node-level admission for DaemonSets that do high-volume logging (policy + liveness to prevent noisy reloads).
- Improve tests for log-collector DaemonSet to include config-reload fuzzing to catch log spam regressions.

Runbook draft (for fast reuse next time):
- Pager triggers: node_filesystem_available_bytes < 1GB OR node.NodeCondition DiskPressure true across >= 3 nodes in 5m.
- Initial checklist (first 10 minutes):
  1. Identify nodes: kubectl get nodes -o wide --selector=role=worker | grep -i DiskPressure
  2. For one affected node: ssh -> sudo du -hs /var/log/journal /var/lib/kubelet /var/lib/containerd | sort -h
  3. Check journald: sudo journalctl --disk-usage ; sudo journalctl --since "10 minutes ago" | grep -E "log-collector|rotate|error"
  4. If journald growth confirmed: rotate+vacuum (journalctl --rotate; journalctl --vacuum-size=500M) and consider rolling back logging DaemonSet.
  5. If container runtime GC is blocked: check containerd logs (sudo journalctl -u containerd -n 200) and restart containerd if GC stuck.
  6. Cordons and drains: target nodes with highest disk usage first; avoid draining more than 2 nodes in the same AZ simultaneously.

Commands to keep handy (copy/paste):
- Check disk by directory: sudo du -sh /var/log/journal /var/lib/kubelet /var/lib/containerd /var/lib/docker | sort -h
- Rotate + vacuum journal: sudo journalctl --rotate && sudo journalctl --vacuum-size=500M
- Find top journald consumers by pid: sudo journalctl --output=json | jq -r '.SYSLOG_IDENTIFIER' | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head -n 20
- Restart containerd: sudo systemctl restart containerd && sudo journalctl -u containerd -f --no-pager

Postmortem notes (for final):
- We should convert this doc into a full postmortem if root cause confirmed (daemonset bug + journald config). Include timeline, customer impact, and RCA.
- Cross-team follow-up: Eng-sre + infra + logging team to coordinate: hotfix rollout, AMI bake changes, CI test for logging reloads.

Notes to self / informal observations:
- On a few nodes, journal vacuum returned little free space because deleted journal files were still held by a process; lsof showed journald files held by pid 1 (systemd) until rotate; confirm vacuum actually frees on these AMIs.
- We observed a pattern that our kubelet's image GC has poor heuristics when overlayfs is under heavy churn; may need to tune imageGCLowThresholdPercent / imageGCHighThresholdPercent.
- TODO: follow up with logging team to request a feature flag to disable verbose reload logging by default.

Appendix (raw excerpts from logs):
- journald excerpt (truncated):
  Nov 11 06:14:02 worker-az2 log-collector[1998]: reloader: config reload start
  Nov 11 06:14:03 worker-az2 log-collector[1998]: reloader: config reload done
  Nov 11 06:14:03 worker-az2 log-collector[1998]: rotate: starting rotation
  Nov 11 06:14:03 worker-az2 log-collector[1998]: rotate: error: failed to close file descriptor (retries: 20)
  Nov 11 06:14:03 worker-az2 log-collector[1998]: rotate: retrying in 50ms
  (these lines repeated thousands of times)

- kubelet eviction excerpt:
  Nov 11 06:16:10 eviction manager: "nodefs available: 48Mi < eviction threshold 100Mi"
  Nov 11 06:16:11 eviction manager: "evicting pod..." pod=namespace/app-5cd4f

Next steps before final postmortem:
- Collect full node-level metrics and attach to final (disk usage over last 24h, journal growth rate).
- Verify containerd GC metrics and capture strace if we can reproduce on a staging node.
- Schedule a follow-up retro with Logging team + Infra on 2024-11-18.

End of oncall notes (draft).
